Derive the invariant
Plan a concrete model of the mathematical relationship in this exercise.
Fix the reference whole and the unit. Compute the exact relationship before
selecting the model and write the answer in the form requested by the item.
Check the bank answer, each selected option and the nearest plausible error.
Where rounding is requested, keep the exact value and use the approximation
sign for the rounded representation.

Choose a representation
- Fractions and division: use an equal-width strip divided into the actual
  denominator's equal parts. Show exactly the numerator's count. For
  equivalent fractions, align the whole lengths and the shaded boundaries.
- Decimal place value: use a place-value table or the same number-line point.
  Show that 0.2 and 0.20 occupy the same point. On a number line, mark values
  in increasing order with equal steps and consistent units.
- Percent conversions: show the same portion of one whole. For example,
  0.25 = 25/100 = 25% can use a four-part strip with one equal part shaded.
  If the task needs hundredths, label a 10-by-10 grid and specify the exact
  shading in full rows or columns when possible.

Hand off one countable diagram
Use scene to record the visual arrangement, the exact equation and one
recall check. Map each anchor to a verifiable relationship, such as one
of four equal parts to 1/4. Keep any distractor comparison on the same scale
and with the same whole. Draw a distractor only when it clarifies the rule.
In image_prompt, give the whole, geometry, total and filled counts, exact
label text and label positions. Verify the scale, partition sizes, equation,
signs and units. Choose a simpler equivalent model when its geometry makes
the same rule easier to count. With search enabled, use supported when the
calculation establishes the answer and retrieved material supports the rule.
